title: Project contexts and delivery methods
blurb: Recognize the commercial, delivery method, organizational and scale contexts, and say where PRINCE2 Agile fits.
question: A project's main products will be built by an outside firm under contract. Which project context does this describe, and why does it matter?

teach.h: Projects never run in a vacuum
teach.body: PRINCE2 Project Management can be used in many situations, and the situation shapes how it is applied. The book names several contexts to consider: the commercial context, the delivery method, the organizational context and the scale of the project. Recognizing them tells you how much formality, which roles and which delivery approach the project needs.

head: Context
The question it raises
Example
rows: Are suppliers outside the sponsoring organization?
Standalone, or part of a programme or portfolio?
One of five projects in a programme
teach.caption: Paraphrased from 1.3.4.

teach.h: Delivery method: where PRINCE2 Agile fits
teach.body: Delivery can be linear-sequential (each phase finished before the next) or iterative-incremental (products evolve through repeated cycles). PRINCE2 Project Management is configured to work with any chosen delivery method. PRINCE2 Agile is specifically designed for projects that use iterative and incremental, that is agile, delivery.

bands.label: Large, complex: formal governance, tight tolerances

teach.caption: Scale influences governance formality, documentation, project structure and tolerances (1.3.4).

teach.body: Haldon Libraries is building a digital lending app. It is one of four projects in the council's digital programme (organizational). An external agency builds the app under contract (commercial). The team delivers in two-week iterations with frequent releases (delivery method), so project manager Ruth Adeyemi chooses PRINCE2 Agile. With one team and a modest budget (scale), the board keeps reporting light: a project dashboard rather than long reports.

teach.text: Do not say PRINCE2 Project Management only works with linear delivery. It can host any delivery method. It is PRINCE2 Agile that is designed specifically for iterative and incremental delivery. Also, 'organizational context' is about programme, portfolio or standalone, not about the project's internal team structure.

items: Commercial context: suppliers may be external to the sponsoring organization.
Delivery method: linear-sequential or iterative-incremental; PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative-incremental.
Organizational context: standalone, or part of a programme or portfolio.
Scale: drives formality of governance, documentation, structure and tolerances.

summary: You can now recognize the commercial, delivery method, organizational and scale contexts in a description. You can also explain that PRINCE2 Project Management supports any delivery method while PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative-incremental delivery.

A.q: Which project context reminds you that the suppliers of a project's products may be external to the sponsoring organization?
A.why: The commercial context considers that suppliers may be external to the sponsoring organization (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: Organizational context is about being standalone or part of a programme or portfolio.
whyNot.1: Delivery method is about linear-sequential or iterative-incremental work.
whyNot.3: Scale is about how simple or complex the project is.

A.q: For which kind of delivery is PRINCE2 Agile specifically designed?
A.why: PRINCE2 Agile is specifically designed for projects using iterative and incremental (agile) delivery (1.3.4).

whyNot.1: Linear-sequential delivery is handled by PRINCE2 Project Management, not the design focus of PRINCE2 Agile.
whyNot.2: Supporting any delivery method describes PRINCE2 Project Management.
whyNot.3: External suppliers are a commercial context, not a delivery method.

A.q: A project is one of several in a programme run by a regional health board. Which context does this describe?
A.why: Organizational context covers whether a project is part of a programme or portfolio or is standalone (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: Commercial context is about suppliers external to the sponsoring organization.
whyNot.1: Scale is about size and complexity, not where the project sits.
whyNot.2: Delivery method is about how the work is delivered.

B.q: Which statement about PRINCE2 Project Management and delivery methods is correct?
options: It needs iterative delivery before it can be applied
It can be used with any chosen delivery method
It replaces the delivery method with its processes
It suits linear delivery and cannot host agile
B.why: PRINCE2 Project Management is configured to enable a project to implement any chosen delivery method (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: It works with linear-sequential and iterative-incremental delivery.
whyNot.2: Its processes manage the project; the delivery method is how products are built.
whyNot.3: It can host any delivery method, including agile; PRINCE2 Agile specializes in agile.

B.q: A board decides that a large, multi-site project needs more formal governance and tighter tolerances than its usual small projects. Which context drives this decision?
B.why: Scale influences how a project is managed and controlled, including governance formality and tolerances (1.3.4).

whyNot.2: Organizational context concerns programme, portfolio or standalone.
whyNot.3: Delivery method concerns linear or iterative delivery, not formality.

B.q: A project plans to build its product in a series of short cycles, releasing working increments for feedback. Which context is being described?
B.why: The delivery method is the way project work is delivered, here iterative-incremental (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: Organizational context is about where the project sits (programme, portfolio, standalone).
whyNot.1: Commercial context is about suppliers external to the sponsor.
whyNot.3: Scale is about the project's size and complexity.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. A standalone project and a programme project differ in organizational context.
2. PRINCE2 Agile is designed for linear-sequential delivery.
3. Scale influences the formality of documentation and tolerances.
4. Commercial context is about whether the team uses Scrum or Kanban.
C.why: Statement 1 matches the organizational context and statement 3 the scale context (1.3.4).

whyNot.1: Both are wrong: PRINCE2 Agile is for iterative-incremental delivery, and Scrum or Kanban is a delivery matter.
whyNot.2: Statement 2 is wrong: PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative and incremental delivery.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the commercial context concerns external suppliers.

C.q: A housing association's project sits inside its asset portfolio, and an outside contractor builds the products. Which two contexts are described?
C.why: Sitting in a portfolio is the organizational context; an outside contractor is the commercial context (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: Neither size nor the way work is delivered is described.
whyNot.1: The outside contractor is commercial, but nothing describes how the work is delivered.
whyNot.2: Portfolio membership is organizational, but nothing describes the project's size.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. PRINCE2 Project Management can implement any chosen delivery method, whereas PRINCE2 Agile is specifically designed for [?] and incremental delivery.
C.why: PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative and incremental (agile) delivery (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: Linear-sequential is the other delivery method, not the one PRINCE2 Agile targets.
whyNot.2: Commercial is a context about suppliers, not a delivery method.
whyNot.3: Scaling agile is a separate topic; the delivery method named is iterative.

reteach.title: Four questions before you tailor
reteach.question: What four questions about context should a project manager ask early?

items: Who builds the products: our own staff or an outside supplier? (commercial)
Will we work in phases or in iterations? (delivery method)
Are we standalone or part of a programme or portfolio? (organizational)
How big and complex are we? (scale)

blocks.text: Iterative delivery is a delivery-method answer, not a scale answer. A contract with a supplier is commercial, not organizational.

explain.body: Suppliers of the project's products may be external to the sponsoring organization, bringing contracts and their own interests (1.3.4).

test.q: A council hires an external firm to build its new parking app. Which context does this mainly illustrate?
test.why: An external supplier building the products is the commercial context (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: Organizational context is about programme, portfolio or standalone.
whyNot.1: Scale is about size and complexity.
whyNot.2: Delivery method is about how the work is delivered.

explain.body: Linear-sequential or iterative-incremental. PRINCE2 Project Management supports any; PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative-incremental (1.3.4).

test.q: Which statement correctly contrasts PRINCE2 Project Management and PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Both are designed for linear-sequential delivery
PRINCE2 7 hosts any method; Agile targets iterative
PRINCE2 7 needs agile delivery; Agile hosts any
Neither treats the delivery method as a context
test.why: PRINCE2 Project Management can implement any delivery method, and PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative-incremental delivery (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative and incremental delivery.
whyNot.3: Delivery method is a named context both consider.

explain.body: A project may be standalone, introducing a single change, or part of a programme or portfolio (1.3.4).

test.q: Which context covers whether a project is standalone or part of a programme or portfolio?

whyNot.1: Commercial context is about external suppliers.
whyNot.2: Delivery method is about linear or iterative work.
whyNot.3: Scale is about how simple or complex the project is.

explain.body: Projects range from simple to large and complex. Scale shapes governance formality, documentation, structure and tolerances (1.3.4).

test.q: Which aspect of managing a project does the scale context influence?
options: The agile mindset of the team
test.why: Scale influences governance formality, documentation, project structure and tolerances (1.3.4).

whyNot.0: Mindset is a people matter, not set by scale.
whyNot.1: A supplier's business case relates to the commercial context.
whyNot.3: Programme membership is the organizational context.
